title: More Than the Hurt
north_star: A soft illustrated archive of Aachu and Zuv's love, chaos, culture, and tiny rituals.

golden_theme_contract.first_principles_rule: Before submitting or scoring any new carousel idea, use these source files as the first-principles explanation of why the gold carousel worked: universal anti-ideal -> concrete Aachu proof -> Zuv steady response -> tender acceptance thesis.
golden_theme_contract.rule: Every carousel must start from a universal relationship truth, then prove it through Aachu/Zuv specifics. Photos, places, outfits, and objects are evidence, not the premise.
hard_fail_if: The concept is primarily about an object, outfit, location, or photo aesthetic.
A stranger could not send the carousel to a partner without knowing the private photo context.
Aachu's expressive role is missing or mocked.
Zuv's calm role is passive, absent, or treated as background.
The concept is mostly about taking photos, looking beautiful, glowing, or waiting for one more picture without a deeper relationship tension.
One partner's role is only looking good while the other waits or holds things.
The final thesis is generic romance without a concrete proof trail.
default_five_slide_map: Universal hook: one swipe-stopping relationship truth.
Aachu-specific reveal: her version of the truth.
Concrete proof: a drawable behavior, object, or ritual from the reference material.
Zuv role: what his calm, patience, care, or choice does emotionally.
Save/share thesis: the tender truth underneath the joke.
caption_formula: Open with the universal relationship truth.
Show the couple-specific behavior, care, posture, object, or rhythm in the middle; name Aachu/Zuv only when natural.
End with a soft send/save-worthy thesis.

successful_carousel_standard.rule: Build a public identity mirror with concrete couple receipts, active Zuv care, an emotional reversal, and a send/save thesis; stage the story in visible actions before choosing poster text; do not optimize for keywords.
successful_carousel_standard.open_reasoning_policy: Expose the real goal and selection logic; do not optimize for keywords or let slide copy substitute for staged story action.
successful_carousel_standard.prompt_rule: Prompts must prove relationship behavior through stage-scene Aachu/Zuv action; text completes the scene instead of carrying it.

human_truth: A repairable hurt can become so visually dominant that one painful act starts standing in for a whole person. Accountability does not erase the act; it makes it possible to see the person without denying what happened.
emotional_arc: broken promise -> hurt dominates the frame -> memory is re-edited through pain -> accountability without pressure -> direct re-seeing -> whole-person recognition without erasure
source_story_summary: Locked illustrative story approved by the creator on 2026-08-14: Aachu prepares a simple dinner for two after Zuv promises to be home. Aachu waits beside a cold untouched plate and a burned-low candle -> Zuv arrives late and stops in the doorway -> he sets down his keys and deliberately places his phone face-down instead of reaching or explaining -> the empty chair visually blocks Aachu view of him -> later Aachu turns three shared framed memories face-down -> the following morning Zuv sits in the once-empty chair, keeps his hands open, and waits without forcing forgiveness -> Aachu lifts one frame upright with its plain back toward us and looks at him directly -> Zuv pulls that same chair to the adjacent side so its back leaves their sightline while the cold plate remains visible. The obstacle is a repairable broken promise: hurt risks flattening one whole person into one painful act. The reversal is accountability without pressure, not erasure or a grand gesture. Send this to the partner when you need to say: what you did hurt me, but I am trying not to make that moment your entire identity. Safety boundary: this is not about repeated harm, cruelty, coercion, abuse, or betrayal.
visual_style: Create a premium hand-drawn romantic watercolor-and-ink @a.storyof.two Instagram post illustration in native 3:4 portrait composition by default: generate the source at 1440x1920 and export proportionally to exact 1080x1440 final. Generate separate native 9:16 artwork at 1080x1920 only when the creator explicitly requests Reel or Story; never add it as an automatic companion output. Always use config/references/a-story-illustration-master-prompt.md, config/references/a-story-premium-illustration-style-lock.md, and the style bundle in config/references/style-lock/observational-intimacy-premium/. Use shared images only as mood/composition references unless the creator explicitly says otherwise or the images clearly depict the requested people/couple for this prompt; in that case, treat them as current-request identity references for faces, expressions, posture, wardrobe anchors, and relationship energy. Preserve their emotional essence, copy, message, story, gesture, objects, and requested composition, but never let an external reference style take over. Use the Aachu/Zuv identity reference as the face and wardrobe anchor always. Identity reference images are the highest-priority face source: preserve the same recurring real-person Aachu/Zuv faces, expressions, warm medium-brown South Asian skin tones, Aachu's expressive dark eyes and long dark wavy hair, and Zuv's curly dark hair, strong brows, dark almond eyes, defined nose, short natural stubble, and gentle smile. Previous successful illustrations are style references only: use them for warm ivory paper, visible paper grain, fine ink and pencil linework, transparent watercolor blooms, delicate sketch texture, muted vintage palette, tactile clothing detail, soft faded edges, lower/middle-lower couple placement, and generous clean upper-middle negative space. Render exact handwritten text in upper-middle negative space, matching the approved handwritten font styles from the reference images. Every final illustration must include only the tiny low-contrast handwritten brandmark '@a.storyof.two' in the top-right as part of the paper artwork. No photorealism, no UI, no random text, no quote-card design. Scene logic and pose anatomy are hard gates: clothing, props, and body action must prove the exact copy, and any visible people must look natural, flattering, and physically believable.
target_voice: Aachu/Zuv archive voice: warm, specific, playful underneath the tenderness

stage_scene_gate.consequence: The cold plate, dead candle, and two downturned frames remain as evidence that repair does not erase harm.

carousel_story_director_persona.source_story: Locked illustrative story approved by the creator on 2026-08-14: Aachu prepares a simple dinner for two after Zuv promises to be home. Aachu waits beside a cold untouched plate and a burned-low candle -> Zuv arrives late and stops in the doorway -> he sets down his keys and deliberately places his phone face-down instead of reaching or explaining -> the empty chair visually blocks Aachu view of him -> later Aachu turns three shared framed memories face-down -> the following morning Zuv sits in the once-empty chair, keeps his hands open, and waits without forcing forgiveness -> Aachu lifts one frame upright with its plain back toward us and looks at him directly -> Zuv pulls that same chair to the adjacent side so its back leaves their sightline while the cold plate remains visible. The obstacle is a repairable broken promise: hurt risks flattening one whole person into one painful act. The reversal is accountability without pressure, not erasure or a grand gesture. Send this to the partner when you need to say: what you did hurt me, but I am trying not to make that moment your entire identity. Safety boundary: this is not about repeated harm, cruelty, coercion, abuse, or betrayal.
